newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-OPENERS PLACE SRI LANKA IN STRONG POSITION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-OPENERS PLACE SRI LANKA IN STRONG POSITION.

text.p: Sri Lanka's opening bowlers and batsmen combined on Monday to put the home side in a strong position on the third day of the second test.

At the close, Sanath Jayasuriya and Russell Arnold had consolidated some good work from pacemen Chaminda Vaas and Sajeeva de Silva by sharing an unfinished partnership of 102 to give Sri Lanka an overall lead of 141.
The first test in the two-test series was drawn.
Jayasuriya was undefeated on 61 scored off 123 balls with six fours, his third half-century in the series, and Arnold, playing in only his second test, was not out 29.

Pakistan's attack was depleted by the absence of their fast bowlers Mohammad Zahid and Shahid Nazir, both suffering from back injuries. Pakistan also lost the services of wicketkeeper Moin Khan who retired hurt with a painful right heel.
Sri Lanka capitalised on these injuries to take a first innings lead of 39 with left-armers Vaas and Sajeeva de Silva taking nine wickets between them to dismiss Pakistan for 292 by tea.
Sri Lanka took the last four Pakistan wickets for 16 runs, three of them being claimed by de Silva, who in his second test finished with an innings haul of five for 85.
The 26-year-old quick bowler did not take a wicket in his only previous test, against New Zealand at Hamilton early this year..
Using the second new ball to good effect, de Silva produced a hostile spell to run through the Pakistani low-order after left-arm spinner Jayantha Silva had dismissed top scorer Moin for 98.

The Pakistan wicketkeeper played an exhilarating innings, taking only 109 balls with three sixes and nine fours in a stay of 175 minutes. He was out two short of his fourth test century when he back cut a ball into Marvan Attpattu's hands at point. At 43, he passed 1,000 runs in test cricket.

Moin and Asif Mujtaba, who hit a sedate 49 in 274 minutes, added 91 for the sixth wicket. Mujtaba was out in the third over after lunch, pulling a Vaas long hop to long leg where Aravinda de Silva, running to his left, held a superb catch.
